- Added that saved approvals can be listed and removed through the server API (`GET /api/permission/saved`, `DELETE /api/permission/saved/:id`).
- Fixed the example pattern from `git status*` to the actual saved form, `git status *`.

title: fix(desktop): authenticate SSH servers over one connection
body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51182

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Connecting to an SSH server from the desktop app on Windows asks for the password once for every bootstrap command, then again for the tunnel: four prompts on a typical reconnect, more on a cold start. Windows OpenSSH has no `ControlMaster`, so each `ssh.exe` authenticates again.

This PR uses a single authenticated connection per connect attempt instead of replaying answers to askpass prompts:

- One long-lived `ssh … -D 127.0.0.1:<port> host sh -l -s` process per attempt. It sends a small POSIX driver that reads length-prefixed frames on stdin. Each bootstrap step (discover, version, probe, install/upload, start) runs

Run every bootstrap step and the HTTP forward through one long-lived ssh
process, so password, OTP, and passphrase prompts appear once per connect

Based on prior work in https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/732, the Local Shell Tool was nearly complete but still didn’t work in practice. This PR finishes the logic, adds tests, and provides a working example.
    
## Changes 
    
1. Return tool output to the LLM

    The local command ran, but its **output was not returned to the LLM**. This PR sends the output back, as described in the Local Shell guide: [https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-local-shell](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-local-shell)
    
2. Use `call_id` 

    Upstream (openai-python) `LocalShellCallOutput` uses **`id`**, but the server actually expects **`call_id`**. This PR sets `call_id` so the server accepts the output. A small type-check ignore workaround is include

+import asyncio
+import os
+import subprocess
+
+from agents import Agent, LocalShellCommandRequest, LocalShellTool, Runner, trace
+
+
+def shell_executor(request: LocalShellCommandRequest) -> str:
+    args = request.data.action
+
+    try:
+        completed = subprocess.run(
+            args.command,
+            cwd=args.working_directory or os.getcwd(),
+            env={**os.environ, **args.env} if args.env else os.environ,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=(args.timeout_ms / 1000) if args.timeout_ms else None,
+        )
+        return completed.stdout + completed.stderr
+

+        return "Command execution timed out"
+    except Exception as e:
+        return f"Error executing command: {str(e)}"
+

+        instructions="You are a helpful assistant that can execute shell commands.",
+        model="codex-mini-latest",  # Local shell tool requires a compatible model
+        tools=[LocalShellTool(executor=shell_executor)],
+    )
+

+        result = await Runner.run(
+            agent,
+            "List the files in the current directory and tell me how many there are.",
+        )
+        print(result.final_output)
+
+

+    asyncio.run(main())

title: fix(managed-agent): settle the monitor loop when its resume finds a settled record
body:
## What this PR does

When a Hosted Monitor watch ends before its observation loop registers, the publisher settles the record itself through its no-observer path. If that settle lands while a tool turn is resuming the watch, the resume already saw the terminal record and returned early — but the loop stayed registered without ever being marked finished. The Session close then stopped that loop by writing a second terminal revision to a record that was already terminal, which the record contract refuses. This change marks the loop ended and settled at that early return, so the close's stop on such a loop is a no-op.

## Why it's needed

The refused second settle escaped the Session close, which answered `503 managed_session_close_failed`. For a `stop_requested` close the first attempt fail

title: Fix Gemini Model Integration Issues (#2803)
body:
# Fix Gemini Model Integration Issues

Fixes #2803

## Description

This PR addresses the issue where Google Gemini models fail in CrewAI due to LiteLLM API key and model parsing issues. The fix handles two main problems:

1. **API Key Mapping**: LiteLLM expects `GEMINI_API_KEY` but users typically set `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. This PR adds automatic mapping from `GOOGLE_API_KEY` to `GEMINI_API_KEY` when using Gemini models.

2. **Model Name Normalization**: Model formats like "models/gemini-pro" or "gemini-pro" aren't parsed correctly as provider/model. This PR adds normalization to ensure all Gemini model names are in the correct format for LiteLLM (gemini/model-name).

## Changes

- Added `_is_gemini_model` method to detect Gemini models
- Added `_normalize_gemini_model` method to handle differ

The two slowest jobs in the PR test fan-out are a pair of co-leaders that finish within ~15s of each other, so whichever ends last gates every PR: the `E2E Test (packages/*)` job runs as a single unsharded matrix value at **~306s P50**, and the `E2E kitchen-sink` Playwright job runs 3 shards whose slowest sits at **~291s P50**. This PR fixes a Windows 10 specific issue where F5 debugging was being blocked by an unnecessary await in the HMR (Hot Module Replacement) server check.

 ```ts
body:
Fixes the user-visible error in #64628. The root cause in that session isn't confirmed yet.

## Problem

Gemini rejects any request whose `contents` end on a `model` turn:

```

```
`lowerMessages` in `packages/ai/src/protocols/gemini.ts` lowers whatever history it gets. Unanswered local tool calls are already answered with `Tool result missing` by `normalizeToolHistory`. So the tail that reaches Gemini is an assistant message with text or reasoning only.

When a sub-agent used as a managed agent hits a tool error and loops, or exhausts max_steps, MultiStepAgent.run() never raises: it falls back to a best-effort, LLM-generated answer via provide_final_answer() instead. title: fix(checkpoint): evaluate LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK at use time instead of import time
```
body:
Fixes #7847

## Summary

`LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK` is documented as a security control that restricts msgpack checkpoint deserialization to a built-in allowlist of safe types. However, the env var is only read once at module import time. Applications that set the env var during startup (after a dependency has already imported `_msgpack`) get permissive deserialization silently.

## Problem

```python
# _msgpack.py — evaluated once at import time
STRICT_MSGPACK_ENABLED = os.getenv("LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK", "false").lower() in (...)
```

If any code path imports `langgraph.checkpoint.serde._msgpack` before `os.environ["LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK"] = "true"` executes, the strict mode is permanently off for the lifetime of the process. This is easy to hit when an app sets env vars in `main()`
